content.user_title: Build a CEO Personal Operating System
content.value_statement: Executives often lose insight across reviews, goals, and leadership decisions. This skill builds a structured private system for reflection, planning, and pattern tracking.
actual_capabilities: Creates a `ceo-personal-os` folder structure with reviews, goals, frameworks, interviews, memory, and uploads sections.
Builds framework files from the included leadership, startup, time, and human-scale business references.
Provides daily, weekly, quarterly, and annual review cadences with focused executive prompts.
Uses interview scripts for stress patterns, time audits, customer development, team reflection, and failure detection.
Extracts patterns from uploaded past reviews and records them in `memory.md` for future reflection.
Structures 1-year, 3-year, and 10-year goals alongside a three-year vivid vision process.
limitations: It is a reflection system, not a task manager, calendar, or project tracker.
It depends on user-supplied context and honest review inputs.
It does not replace therapy, legal advice, financial advice, or executive coaching.
It creates local markdown material and does not provide automatic integrations.

use_cases.title: Install a Founder Reflection System
use_cases.description: Create a private workspace for reviews, goals, principles, and decision patterns before a new operating cadence begins.

use_cases.title: Run Quarterly Leadership Reviews
use_cases.description: Use coaching questions and business frameworks to examine team health, time use, customer learning, and venture risk.

use_cases.title: Synthesize Past Reviews
use_cases.description: Summarize past review documents, identify repeated patterns, and preserve useful insights for future planning.

prompt_templates.title: Create My Personal OS
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a CEO personal operating system for me. Use the default folder structure, review cadences, goals, frameworks, and interview scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Weekly Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a weekly review for me. Focus on energy, time leaks, meaningful progress, delegation, and one priority for next week.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Venture Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Eisenmann, Blank, Collins, and Campbell frameworks to review my company risks this quarter. Ask questions first, then summarize patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Patterns From Past Reviews
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the past reviews in uploads. Extract repeated goals, failures, strengths, decision patterns, and unresolved themes. Update memory.md with concise insights.

output_examples.input: Run a weekly review focused on time and energy.
output: A short review with energy rating, one win, one friction point, and one priority for next week.
A time audit that separates draining work, energizing work, low-value tasks, and high-value tasks.
A delegation prompt that identifies one task to audit, transfer, or stop.

output_examples.input: Help me plan a quarterly founder review.
output: A structured session covering team development, failure patterns, customer learning, operating role, and long-term purpose.
A summary of risks, open questions, and decisions that need direct attention.
A short next-quarter focus list linked to goals and leadership principles.

output_examples.input: Summarize my old annual reviews and find patterns.
output: A concise synthesis of recurring wins, setbacks, energy drains, strengths, and relationship themes.
A memory update with durable patterns that can inform future reviews.
A list of questions to resolve before setting new annual goals.

best_practices: Keep the system private and avoid adding secrets, credentials, or sensitive third-party information.
Run short weekly reviews before long quarterly or annual reviews.
Update memory.md only with durable patterns, not every temporary thought.
anti_patterns: Do not turn the system into a task tracker or calendar clone.
Do not use generic productivity frameworks when the included frameworks are more relevant.
Do not treat reflective prompts as medical, legal, financial, or clinical guidance.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a markdown-based executive reflection system with reviews, goals, frameworks, interview prompts, and pattern memory.

faq.question: Does it run code or install software?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains markdown instructions and reference files. It does not include scripts or executable commands.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it a task management system?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for reflection, planning, pattern recognition, and executive review.

faq.question: What should I upload?
faq.answer: Upload past reviews or planning notes only when you want pattern extraction. Remove secrets and sensitive third-party details first.

faq.question: Can it replace an executive coach?
faq.answer: No. It can structure reflection and questions, but it does not replace professional judgment or coaching relationships.
